claims.statement: For the explicitly supplied rational d=2 symmetric broadcaster B=(9/10)B_Z+(1/10)B_U, a seeded 16-round, 1024-sample-per-round finite rational tree-response replay produces a 1088-outcome canonical EB channel Psi with exact certificate I-Psi <= 4(I-Phi)+(1/4)I on all Hermitian matrices.
assumptions: Input is the exact dense rational Liouville matrix in INPUT_BROADCASTER_LIOUVILLE.json.

The sample replay uses exact enumeration of this 16-outcome tree distribution as a diagnostic accelerator; the separately checked recursive conditional sampler is the scalable route in the general compiler argument.
This is a particular finite randomized transcript; its exact final postcheck, rather than a generic concentration-horizon claim, certifies the returned inequality.
claims.status: finite exact computation; not a general theorem or external validation
claims.proof_path: compiler_replay.py and REPLAY.json; full output map in FINAL_CHANNEL.json
costs: d=2; dense broadcaster has 64 complex-rational Liouville entries with aggregate numerator/denominator bit count 234.
T=16, N=1024, delta=1/4, gamma=1/100, alpha=1/10, seed=20261008; 256 additional recursive sampler draws.
The exact 16-outcome tree was enumerated for this diagnostic run; runtime with serialization and exact rechecks was about 75.5 seconds in SymPy 1.14.
The generic sufficient MW horizon at these parameters is 18000 rounds; sample formula coefficient is about 533.28 times an unspecified absolute concentration constant.

claims.statement: For every L>=1, the product marginal Phi_L=Phi_1^{tensor L} of the supplied repeated local symmetric qubit broadcaster has a succinct product canonical EB comparator Psi_L=Psi_1^{tensor L} satisfying I-Psi_L <= 2(I-Phi_L) on every Hermitian mode, with equality on a single-site Z Pauli mode and identities elsewhere.
assumptions: The global input is supplied in exact product/tensor-factorized form as L copies of B_1; the compiler need not construct the dense 2^L-channel matrix.
The local maps are Phi_1=(9/10)Delta_Z+(1/10)Gamma, with Pauli eigenvalues (1/15,1/15,29/30), and Psi_1=(14/15)Delta_Z+(1/15)Depolarizing, with eigenvalues (0,0,14/15).
The proof covers the complete tensor-product Pauli basis, including the identity, rather than a selected low-energy observable set.
claims.status: internally derived exact structured theorem; product closure was previously identified, and no priority claim is made
costs: Homogeneous rational input has one local 16x4 broadcaster descriptor plus site count L; applying the local measure-and-prepare instrument costs O(L).
The succinct global output is a tensor product of local three-outcome instruments; a flattened global POVM has 3^L outcome strings and is intentionally not emitted.
For L=64, global Hilbert dimension is 2^64 while the local instrument still has three effects.
claims.falsifier: A local transfer-matrix error, failure of the canonical POVM sums, or a product Pauli word violating the exact factor-2 inequality.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether local structure can be relaxed to bounded treewidth, sparse couplings, or a certified low-energy invariant subspace while preserving an all-mode comparator or a clearly stated restricted promise family.
claims.novelty_boundary: The qubit comparator and tensor-product closure are inherited from earlier internal work. The added consequence is a succinct repeated-local compiler representation and its all-mode near-fixed EB error bound; this is not an arbitrary-channel factor-2 proof.

claims.statement: For every tensor product of qubit broadcasters B_i=theta_i B_{Z,n_i}+(1-theta_i)B_U with rational theta_i in [1/4,1] and n_i in {X,Y,Z}, a product canonical EB comparator satisfies I-Psi <= 2(I-Phi) on the full Hermitian space. A seven-site heterogeneous instance is checked exactly over every distinct spectral-type word.
assumptions: The broadcaster is supplied as a product of local symmetric broadcasters; each local axis is one of X/Y/Z and each local strength is a rational in [1/4,1].
The comparator at site i is Psi_i=alpha_i Delta_{n_i}+(1-alpha_i) Depolarizing with alpha_i=(1+2 theta_i)/3; the global comparator is the tensor product.
The all-L proof uses the complete tensor eigenoperator basis and the product lemma; no global dense channel or flattened POVM is constructed.
claims.status: internally derived exact structured theorem plus finite exact replay; no priority claim
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, Heterogeneous axes and site strengths; all-L product lemma
costs: Finite test has L=7, global dimension 128, and checks all 3^7 distinct spectral-type words exactly; the transverse category represents both transverse eigenoperators.
Input and output use O(L) local records/instruments plus the exact rational bit lengths; applying the product instrument uses O(L) local operations.
A globally flattened three-outcome instrument would have 3^L outcomes and is not emitted; physical product measurement on entangled inputs retains correlated outcome statistics.
claims.falsifier: A local broadcaster/comparator transfer mismatch, a failed canonical POVM sum, or any exact tensor eigenvalue pair violating the factor-2 inequality.

claims.statement: Any supplied L-site product of the local symmetric broadcasters in the heterogeneous product theorem, dressed by the same supplied unitary circuit U on the input and each receiver, has an EB comparator dressed in the same way and satisfying I-Psi_U <= 2(I-Phi_U) on the full Hermitian space. A two-site CNOT instance is exactly replayed and its marginal is proved nonproduct.
assumptions: The undressed product broadcaster factors and local parameter/axis promises are supplied and checked as in C4-C7-HETEROGENEOUS-LOCAL-FACTOR2-COMPILER.
The same unitary U is applied before the product broadcaster on the input and after it on both receivers.
For the O(LD) claim, U is supplied as a depth-D bounded-range circuit; no general efficient simulation claim is made for arbitrary dense U.
